summary.text: Seismic imaging studies Earth's internal structure using how seismic waves, mechanical waves that travel through the planet, are refracted and reflected.
Body waves follow paths set by the density and stiffness of the rock, which depend on its temperature, composition and phase.
Because S waves cannot pass through liquids, their absence in Earth's outer core suggests the outer core is liquid.

facts.label: Speed at the core
facts.value: Drops sharply from mantle to outer core

items.prompt: Seismic stations in several cities each note when the different wave types from one quake arrive. What can scientists work out from those timing gaps?

options.label: How old the broken fault is
When the next quake will strike
Where the quake started underground
How hot the inner core is

items.explain: Earthquakes produce wave types with different speeds, and their different travel times let scientists locate the quake's hypocenter.

items.prompt: Why are S waves absent in Earth's outer core?

options.label: It is liquid, and liquids cannot carry shear
It is too dense for any wave to cross
Its magnetic field absorbs them
It is too cold for them to move

items.explain: S waves travel only through solids because fluids do not support shear stresses, so their absence in the outer core suggests it is liquid.

items.prompt: A large earthquake strikes far away. Which kind of wave reaches the seismograph first?

options.label: S waves
Rayleigh waves
Love waves
P waves

items.explain: P waves travel faster than other waves through Earth, so they arrive first; that is why they are called primary.

items.prompt: Why do surface waves tend to cause more damage than body waves?

options.label: They travel much faster than body waves
They move the ground more and fade more slowly
They pass through the core and gain energy
They only happen in the largest quakes

items.explain: Surface waves decay more slowly with distance and have larger particle motion than body waves, so they tend to cause more damage.

items.prompt: A body wave bends as it passes into rock of a different temperature and composition. Which everyday effect is this most like?

options.label: An echo bouncing off a cliff
A siren's pitch changing as it passes
Light bending as it enters water
A magnet pulling on iron filings

items.explain: Body-wave paths are controlled by density and stiffness, which vary with temperature, composition and phase, an effect that resembles the refraction of light.

items.prompt: When a P wave passes out of the ground and into the air, what form does it take?

options.label: Sound
Light
Wind
Heat

items.explain: In air, P waves take the form of sound waves and travel at the speed of sound.

pack.title: Seeing Through Solid Rock
pack.question: How do earthquake waves reveal what lies inside Earth?

beats.title: Seeing Through Solid Rock
beats.hook: One kind of earthquake wave never shows up in Earth's outer core, and that absence gives away what the core is like.

beats.prompt: A large earthquake strikes far away, and a seismograph records several kinds of wave. Which arrives first?
beats.explain: P waves travel faster than other waves through Earth and reach seismograph stations first; S waves follow after them.

choices.label: All of them at once
choices.feedback: Each wave type has its own speed, so they spread out in time.

choices.label: Surface waves
choices.feedback: Surface waves do the most damage, but they travel more slowly than body waves.

choices.label: S waves
choices.feedback: S waves are real body waves, but they are slower and arrive after the P waves.

beats.prompt: Match each wave to the way it moves the ground

right.label: Compress and stretch along the wave's path
Shift the ground across the wave's path

beats.explain: P waves are compressional and longitudinal, S waves are transverse and move the ground perpendicular to their direction, and Rayleigh waves move like waves on water.

beats.prompt: Put these waves in order of speed
beats.explain: P waves are fastest, S waves are slower, Love waves run at about 90% of S-wave speed, and Rayleigh waves are usually slightly slower than Love waves.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?

steps.text: An earthquake sends out both P waves and S waves.
S waves travel only through solids, since fluids do not support shear.
S waves are absent in Earth's outer core.
So the outer core must be solid.

beats.explain: Since S waves cannot cross liquids, finding none in the outer core points to a liquid outer core, not a solid one.

beats.idea: Seismic waves travel at different speeds and only some can cross liquid, so their timing and paths reveal Earth's inner structure.
